- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.36+ sentiment) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (especially -1.25+ sentiment) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays in forecast response) — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day sentiment momentum.
- Avoid overcorrection after sharp price drops — model tends to overshoot recovery; cap upward revisions at +3% of prior day’s price.
- Mean-reversion bias in 30-day forecasts — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment-driven volatility amplification — if sentiment >0.40, forecast should be 1–2% tighter than historical volatility-adjusted mean.
